title: The existing title pages are toned down to calm, presentable versions of themselves
goal: The current built-in title pages (Keynote Clean, Soft Gradient Glass, Kinetic Bold, Editorial Serif, Tech Terminal, Behind Glass, Light Leak, Gradient Glow, Stacked Stagger and the lower thirds) are far too busy. Audit each against the restraint of the approved Apple-level mock and tone it down: quieter backgrounds, fewer effects per part, shorter and calmer motion, better type, so every one is presentable and subtle. They stay available under More styles beneath the ten new pages.
notes: User's words (2026-10-18), after viewing the Apple-level mock: "these look so much better. The existing title pages are far too busy so i think we need to audit them and tone them down to make them a little more presentable and more subtle". The card on title-pages-that-look-like-apple-designed-them was resolved b (build all ten, old set under More styles) with these words. Existing set: PhotonzCore/TitleSet.swift (12 built-ins), live backgrounds from title-backgrounds-that-are-alive-auroras-energy, entrances from title-text-visibly-comes-in-and-every-built-in-t. Memory: visual work needs a measured bar the weak version fails, and a reel for the user.
acceptance: Audit first, one row per existing title in the audit: what makes it busy (background motion speed and contrast, number of effects per part, travel distance, bounce/spin/flip/3D, glows, grain, colour count, type size contrast, timing) measured from its frames, compared with the rules the approved mock follows (docs/design/mocks/pages/video-titles-apple.html and title-pages-that-look-like-apple-designed-them's review: fade, rise of 10 to 22 px, blur in, tracking settle, per-line mask reveal, 600 to 950 ms expo out, outs 300 to 450 ms, one accent colour at most, still or barely moving backgrounds)

Each existing title is revised to those rules while keeping its own identity (Editorial stays editorial, Tech Terminal stays a terminal): at most one effect per part, travel under 24 px, no spring, flip or 3D builds by default, backgrounds slowed to barely moving and lowered in contrast (live backgrounds at about a third of today's speed and strength unless the look needs less), glows and grain subtle or off, typography using the new tracking and line height settings

VISUAL BAR, MEASURED: for each title, background motion (mean pixel difference between frames 0.5 s apart) at most half of today's, and the busyness numbers in the audit all within the mock's ranges; a side by side contact sheet before and after for each, plus a reel
They are grouped under More styles below the ten new pages (per the user's card answer b); titles already in documents keep drawing as they were
A decision card links the before/after reel for the user to judge; anything they still call busy is reworked
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: From title-pages-that-look-like-apple-designed-them (2026-10-18): the More Styles grouping is built (Library header and Insert submenu, BuiltInTitle.isMoreStyle), so acceptance item 4's grouping is done; what is left is the toning down itself. Old-set rule tests now run over TitleSetTests.twelve; TitleCalmMockTests is a model for measuring before/after frames.

owns these walks: title-set-light-leak-walk, title-set-keynote-clean-walk, title-set-stacked-stagger-walk, title-set-split-wipe-walk, title-set-soft-gradient-glass-walk, editing-a-title-never-plays-walk, timeline-sub-layer-rows-walk, title-part-rows-retime-walk, video-library-catalog-walk

Adversarial review before building: the busy parts were measured, not guessed (TitleMoreStylesCalmReelTests on the old code, numbers in queue/audits/2026-10-18-calm-more-styles-before.json): five styles turned in 3D or sprang (Kinetic, Editorial, Glass, Stacked, Pill), rises of 36 to 90 pt, live looks at 70 to 100 speed and 55 to 100 strength, grain 20 to 30 on six, strong glows on two, up to six hues. A Premiere/Final Cut editor expects a lower third and a title card that land once and hold still; nothing in the mock needs state the app lacks, so no prerequisite was filed.

Built: TitleSet.swift redesigned to the calm rules (one move per part, rise under 24, ins 360-950 ms on expo, outs 300-450 on sine, no springs/3D, live looks at a third or less, grain off, glows 0.2, one hue family, tracking and leading on every headline). Tests first: TitleMoreStylesCalmTests (rules), TitleMoreStylesCalmFramesTests (measured bar: background motion at most half of before, all twelve pass, e.g. Light Leak 12.8 -> 1.4, Keynote 8.3 -> 2.0, Terminal 6.0 -> 2.6), TitleSetTests/TitleDesignTests/TitleEntranceInkTests/TitlePartTimingTests/TitleBackgroundsTests restated to the calm timing. Full suite 13,744 passed. All 39 walks that use the older styles pass after updating three walks' timing numbers and the catalog walk's first tile (Keynote Section now leads the shelf).

Pictures looked at: the before/after contact sheet (every after row quieter, words land with one short move), the reel frames at six points (Soft Glass marble and Light Leak orange wash were still loud on the first pass and were retuned: liquid with no crests at scale 180, deeper leaks at strength 12), the Split Wipe exit crops (words hung past a wiping bar; now the card fades whole), and the probe's own Light Leak capture under More Styles.

Left rough, not filed (each is by design and put to the user on the approval card rather than a task): Kinetic Bold's saturated blue, Gradient Glow's faint aurora streaks, Keynote Clean's dim specks, Terminal's slow grid. TitleMoreStylesCalmReelTests stays as the tool that films any future before/after.
